note: Members are epcoritamab (CD20xCD3, MZL trials unreported), ublituximab (phase 1/2 MZL responses; MZL development stopped with umbralisib) and imvotamab (phase 1 terminated, no MZL data found).
label: Marginal zone lymphoma (CD20 depleters)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year is a proxy: first-in-human start June 2018 (NCT03625037); the paper appeared January 2020.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry dated to first clinical use of the model data.
engagement.note: Cynomolgus monkeys showed deep, lasting B-cell depletion on epcoritamab, IV or SC; no human data yet.
engagement.quote: In cynomolgus monkeys, DuoBody-CD3xCD20 demonstrated profound and long-lasting B-cell depletion from peripheral blood and lymphoid organs, which was comparable after subcutaneous and intravenous administration.

engagement.magnitude_basis: peripheral B-cell depletion, monkey vs patient
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract plus accepted manuscript. Population was mixed relapsed B-NHL (68% DLBCL; one MZL patient of 68); engagement allows any dosed humans. NCT03625037 has no posted results.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: the trial paper cites Engelberts 2020 but does not set monkey and patient depletion side by side. Depletion of CD20+ B cells is read as the drug's own proximal product.
engagement.note: Subcutaneous epcoritamab produced robust, sustained B-cell depletion in relapsed B-NHL, as monkeys predicted.
engagement.quote: Epcoritamab induced robust and sustained B-cell depletion, and CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell activation and expansion, with modest increases in cytokine levels.
engagement.reason: Monkey B-cell depletion recurred in patients

engagement.judgement: Sawas 2017 reports responses, not B-cell counts, so the ADCC readout has no patient counterpart I could find in this context.
engagement.model: Ex-vivo ADCC on patient leukaemia/lymphoma cells (ublituximab vs rituximab)
engagement.note: Low-fucose ublituximab (EMAB-6) killed CLL and lymphoma cells by ADCC better than rituximab; no member B-cell depletion data in MZL patients found.
engagement.quote: Comparative studies between CLL and lymphoma cells coated with EMAB-6 or rituximab indicated that the difference of efficacy was more pronounced at low doses and when target cells expressed fewer CD20 molecules.
engagement.reason: No MZL B-cell depletion readout found

engagement.confidence_note: Conference abstract (Blood supplement). Monkey dosing used IgM CD20xCD3; later work names the cyno-cross-reactive surrogate IGM-2324, so product_in_model false.
engagement.note: IgM CD20xCD3 completely depleted circulating and tissue B cells in monkeys and humanized mice; no human depletion data yet.
engagement.quote: Similarly, bispecific IgM completely depletes circulating B cells in cynomolgus monkeys at doses of 300 mg per kg.
engagement.judgement: Opened at the 2019 abstract, the year the NHL phase 1 (NCT04082936) registered.
engagement.model: IgM CD20xCD3 (imvotamab/IGM-2323 and cyno surrogate) in cynomolgus monkeys, humanized NSG mice and human PBMC cytokine assays

engagement.magnitude_basis: depth of peripheral B-cell depletion, monkey (near-complete) vs RA/SLE patients (insufficient)
engagement.confidence_note: Sponsor press release only; NCT06087406 (RA) and NCT06041568 (SLE) terminated with no posted results; no NHL depletion data found for NCT04082936. Comparison made outside MZL.
engagement.note: Monkeys showed near-complete blood and tissue B-cell depletion; imvotamab's RA/SLE phase 1b depletion was insufficient and development stopped.
engagement.quote: Interim data from the Phase 1b studies of imvotamab in rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus show that the depth and consistency of B cell depletion is insufficient to meet our high bar for success,
engagement.reason: Depletion fell short in dosed patients
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Oyasu 2023 (cyno, near-complete peripheral depletion incl. low-CD20 cells) against the sponsor's RA/SLE readout. Engagement admits any dosed humans; flagged imported_from RA. Tier 5 because no higher-tier record exists.
engagement.model: IgM CD20xCD3 (imvotamab/IGM-2323 and cyno surrogate) in cynomolgus monkeys, humanized NSG mice and human PBMC cytokine assays

dose.confidence_note: Accepted manuscript read. Year is a proxy (first-in-human start 2018). The FDA multidisciplinary review describes the monkey 5-week study but states no human exposure target from it.
dose.judgement: The monkey data were one input to a joint PK/PD model with patient data; the RP2D is that model's output, and no monkey-stated target or tolerability margin is public, so untested.
dose.note: Monkey PK/PD fed a semi-mechanistic model that set the 48 mg dose; no stated exposure target or margin is public.
dose.quote: An integrated semi-mechanistic pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modelling approach, which incorporated preclinical pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic data from cynomolgus monkeys

dose.magnitude_basis: concentration window of peak activity vs plasma levels at 100 mg and 1000 mg
dose.confidence_note: EHA 2022 abstract (HemaSphere supplement, PMC9429641), no DOI. The model was built after phase 1 showed lower responses at 600 and 1000 mg, so a retrodiction. Its prospective test (randomized 100 vs 300 mg phase 2) was never reported: the NHL trial terminated.
dose.note: Bell-shaped in-vitro model placed peak activity at 100 mg plasma levels and loss at 1000 mg, reproducing phase 1's lower high-dose responses.
dose.quote: Interestingly, the concentration range of IGM-2323 resulting in peak activity corresponded to the peak and trough plasma levels in patients following 100 mg dose.
dose.judgement: Retrodiction: the abstract itself states phase 1 had already seen lower response rates at 600 and 1000 mg before the model was fitted, so retro, not same.
dose.model: In-vitro T-cell activation/TDCC/CDC assays fitted to a mechanistic synapse-binding model (imvotamab dose response)

dose.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy: the model used dose-escalation data and set the RP2D before expansion began (2020); first public in Li 2022. FDA BLA 761324 review cites it (per checker), hence model_filed true.
dose.note: PBPK/PD model fitted to monkey and escalation data predicted trimer formation plateaus at 48-96 mg and chose 48 mg.
dose.quote: Model-predicted trimer formation plateaued at doses of 48 to 96 mg. Simulation results suggest that the 48-mg dose may achieve optimal response rates in DLBCL and FL.
dose.judgement: Its own track: an in-silico system distinct from the monkey track that the draft scores untested for dose. The stated regimen target is the 48 mg plateau.
dose.model: Semi-mechanistic PBPK/PD model of epcoritamab trimer formation and tumour response (Genmab)

dose.magnitude_basis: dose at which response plateaus: predicted 48-96 mg vs observed ~48 mg
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Exposure-response in FL (EPCORE NHL-1, NHL-3) from the sponsor; no MZL exposure-response exists. NCT03625037 has no posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov.
dose.note: Patient exposure-response in FL showed response plateauing at 48 mg exposures with flat CRS risk, as the model stated.
dose.quote: Higher epcoritamab exposure was associated with higher efficacy (ORR, CR rate, progression-free survival, overall survival; p < 0.05) with potential response rate plateau at 48-mg exposures.
dose.judgement: Paired by me with Li 2022. The 48 mg regimen was reached in patients (target reached = same); whether it worked in MZL is the efficacy question, untouched here. FL chosen over LBCL because its abstract states the plateau.
dose.model: Semi-mechanistic PBPK/PD model of epcoritamab trimer formation and tumour response (Genmab)

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for the model; FDA BLA 761324 review confirms CDX and one DLBCL PDX. The phase 1 escalation enrolled one MZL patient of 68 (Hutchings 2021) with no MZL result given; MZL phase 2 trials NCT06796998 and NCT06563596 are recruiting.
efficacy.judgement: Year is a proxy for first clinical use. Patient efficacy data in MZL for epcoritamab are not reported, so the track stays untested (unsettled).
efficacy.note: Epcoritamab shrank lymphoma cell-line and DLBCL PDX tumours in humanized mice; no MZL model and no member MZL efficacy readout.
efficacy.quote: DuoBody-CD3xCD20 showed promising anti-tumour activity in vivo, also in the presence of excess levels of a CD20 Ab that competes for binding.
efficacy.reason: One MZL patient; MZL trials unreported

efficacy.model: Ex-vivo ADCC on patient leukaemia/lymphoma cells (ublituximab vs rituximab)
efficacy.note: EMAB-6 (ublituximab) out-killed rituximab ex vivo, most at low CD20; no patient data yet.
efficacy.quote: Comparative studies between CLL and lymphoma cells coated with EMAB-6 or rituximab indicated that the difference of efficacy was more pronounced at low doses and when target cells expressed fewer CD20 molecules.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: activity in rituximab-exposed patients vs predicted ADCC advantage over rituximab
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5412890). Eight MZL patients (3 phase 1, 5 phase 2) among 35; MZL-specific ORR not stated in text, phase 1 table gives MZL best responses CR, CR, PR. NCT01647971 (first posted 2012-07-24) has no posted results.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: MZL is 8/35 of the trial, below the 80% bar, so I score the MZL subset (phase 1 table) at low confidence. Only the direction (activity after rituximab) is tested; superiority over rituximab was not. Paired by me; Sawas cites the ADCC data but does not compare.
efficacy.model: Ex-vivo ADCC on patient leukaemia/lymphoma cells (ublituximab vs rituximab)
efficacy.note: Ublituximab monotherapy gave responses in rituximab-pretreated B-NHL; the three phase 1 MZL patients reached CR, CR and PR.
efficacy.quote: Even considering the variability in sample size across subtypes, notable activity was observed in patients with indolent lymphoma, with 21% (4/19) of patients achieving a CR as their best response.
efficacy.reason: MZL patients responded, as ADCC predicted

patient_trials.quote: Number of Participants With Complete Response Rate (CR) at 8 Weeks Post Single Agent Induction

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; FDA BLA 761324 review confirms first-dose cytokine-associated signs and one death at 1 mg/kg IV.
safety.note: Monkeys showed first-dose cytokine release, lower after SC than IV dosing.
safety.quote: Peak plasma levels of DuoBody-CD3xCD20 were lower and delayed after subcutaneous administration, which was associated with a reduction in plasma cytokine levels compared to intravenous administration, while bioavailability was comparable.

safety.magnitude_basis: cytokine release / CRS after SC dosing
safety.confidence_note: Abstract plus accepted manuscript. Mixed relapsed B-NHL (68% DLBCL, one MZL patient), so imported.
safety.judgement: Paired by me. The monkey predicted cytokine release dampened by SC dosing; patients had frequent low-grade CRS with no grade 3+, which I read as a match.
safety.note: SC epcoritamab caused CRS in 59% of patients, all grade 1-2: cytokine release as predicted, mild on SC.
safety.quote: There were no grade 3 or higher CRS events.
safety.reason: Predicted CRS appeared, mild on SC

safety.note: IgM bispecific gave far less cytokine release than IgG bispecifics in vitro and in monkeys; no patient data yet.
safety.quote: Significantly, IGM-2323 exhibits vastly reduced cytokine release in vitro and in vivo, with at least equivalent T cell dependent killing of CD20-expressing target cells
safety.judgement: Opened at the abstract; the prediction is a named harm (CRS) the monkey and PBMC assays can show, predicted low.
safety.model: IgM CD20xCD3 (imvotamab/IGM-2323 and cyno surrogate) in cynomolgus monkeys, humanized NSG mice and human PBMC cytokine assays

safety.magnitude_basis: CRS frequency/severity, predicted low vs observed low
safety.confidence_note: EHA 2022 abstract (HemaSphere supplement, PMC9429641), no DOI; preliminary phase 1 data, CRS rates not given in the abstract. NCT04082936 terminated without posted results.
safety.note: Phase 1 imvotamab in R/R NHL up to 1000 mg showed low CRS and no ICANS, as the IgM preclinical data predicted.
safety.quote: an excellent safety and tolerability profile up to 1000 mg with low cytokine release syndrome (CRS), no immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) and limited neutropenia
safety.reason: Low CRS in patients, as predicted
safety.judgement: Paired by me: the EHA abstract reports patient safety but does not set it beside the 2019 preclinical cytokine data. Trial is mixed NHL with MZL enrolled, so imported_from NHL.
safety.model: IgM CD20xCD3 (imvotamab/IGM-2323 and cyno surrogate) in cynomolgus monkeys, humanized NSG mice and human PBMC cytokine assays
